investigations.name: autopoiesis
investigations.title: Autopoiesis — Composition of the Cellular Interface
investigations.objective: How does a maintained cellular interface arise from molecular processes? Do metabolism, containment, and replication, mutually wired so each maintains the others, compile into a self-sustaining minimal cell — and does each self-organized function run at coarse, self-organized, and molecular grains behind one interface (Law 4, its second home)?
investigations.claim: The three closure processes (metabolism, containment, replication) compile into a minimal cell whose interface is produced by the coupling itself — enzymes and energy exist only because a coupled process made them, not because they were seeded — and each function is realized by conforming handlers at multiple grains (containment and replication at three, metabolism at two) behind one fixed interface, Law 4''s second worked example. This is the closure pattern demonstrated qualitatively, not a validated autopoietic system.

investigations.name: biomolecular-complementarity
investigations.title: Biomolecular Complementarity
investigations.objective: Do molecular mechanisms compose into nested hierarchical composites (proteins -> complexes -> organelles -> ECM) whose interfaces survive deep nesting, and does a gene-expression cascade wired to the deepest leaves preserve every interface across six levels (Law 2 at the deepest nesting)?
investigations.claim: The six-level nested place graph (membrane/cytoplasm/nucleus/chromosome/chromatin/nucleosome, plus a parallel organelles branch) compiles with a coupled transcription->translation->assembly cascade wired to its deepest stores; the interface is preserved through the deepest nesting (Law 2). Complementarity/selectivity is the paper''s organizing principle for why molecules assemble into this hierarchy, but the executable demonstrates hierarchical assembly, not fitted binding selectivity — no partner-choice or binding-affinity mechanism is built or claimed.

investigations.name: cell-cell-coupling
investigations.title: Cell–Cell Coupling
investigations.objective: When two cell interfaces are coupled through one shared environmental nutrient store, what is coupled is not only state but constraint — does one cell's uptake push the other outside its viable bounds (competition), and can a different handler over the same coupling interface stabilize both (cross-feeding)?
investigations.claim: Two cells over one shared-nutrient interface negotiate viability, not just state: under competition the weaker cell (lower uptake capacity) is driven below its viable band while the stronger persists (cell_a viability → 1.0, cell_b → ~0.0001); under cross-feeding, the same coupling interface with a different handler keeps both cells viable (cell_a and cell_b → 1.0) — two handler environments over one interface (Law 4), the draft itself unchanged (Law 2).

investigations.name: cell-cell-coupling-spatial
investigations.title: Cell–Cell Coupling, Spatial
investigations.objective:
Does the Fig 3 viability-negotiation pattern hold as real spatial multicellularity —
multiple CPM cells sharing one diffusing nutrient field, each running its own dynamic-FBA step
at its own footprint, producing both competitive exclusion and cross-feeding — when the whole
colony is composed from independent frameworks through one N-cell coupling process
(`CpmColonyField`), rather than the lumped two-role, shared-scalar-pool stand-in
`draft-to-living-cell`'s Fig 3 study used?
investigations.claim:
Composing N real CPM cells with one shared, real spatio-flux nutrient field through a
single N-cell coupling process (`CpmColonyField`) reproduces Fig 3's viability-negotiation
pattern as genuine spatial multicellularity, not a scripted or lumped stand-in for it: over
20-tick runs, an uptake-capacity asymmetry alone (glucose_vmax 10 vs 4) drives spatial
competitive exclusion (biomass 237.9 vs 64.5, a 3.69x margin; volume 3511 vs 81 px), while a
different composite over the same coupling process — a localized glucose depot, a fast-diffusing
acetate byproduct, and an acetate-consuming role — sustains a cell that never touches glucose
(local glucose 0.0) purely via a diffusing cross-feeding handoff (local acetate 1.30, biomass
1.25 -> 3.79). Both regimes run through the same process; only the composite's cell roles and
field constants differ, mirroring `draft-to-living-cell/cell-cell-coupling`'s law-4 pattern
(two handler environments negotiate the shared-resource constraint differently over one
interface) at real spatial, per-footprint metabolic resolution.

investigations.name: cell-environment-coupling
investigations.title: Cell–Environment Coupling
investigations.objective: Does the cellular interface become a genuine sense/act loop when the environment is a real diffusing spatial field the cell reads and acts back on?
investigations.claim: Compiling the Fig 5 draft installs a real Laplacian-diffusion field and single-cell uptake; the cell depletes nutrient locally, diffusion refills it, and the cell reshapes the very gradient it depends on (niche construction) — interface preserved (Law 2).

investigations.name: cell-environment-coupling-spatial
investigations.title: Cell–Environment Coupling, Spatial (flagship)
investigations.objective:
Does the Fig 5 sense/act loop hold as real spatial metabolism — one CPM cell sensing
a diffusing nutrient field, running flux-balance analysis at its own footprint, growing, and
secreting a byproduct back into the field — when the cell and its environment are each real,
independently-built simulators (viva-cpm's Cellular Potts engine, spatio-flux's
diffusion-advection and dynamic-FBA processes) composed through one typed coupling process
(`CpmCellField`), rather than a scripted or lumped stand-in for that coupling?
investigations.claim:
Composing a real CPM cell with a real spatio-flux nutrient field through one typed
coupling process (`CpmCellField`) reproduces the Fig 5 sense/act loop as genuine spatial
metabolism, not a scripted stand-in for it: over 20 ticks the cell runs dynamic-FBA at its own
footprint (`e_coli_core`, O2-capped to force acetate overflow), grows ~3.4x in CPM volume (32
-> 110 px, ~3% of a 60x60 lattice it does not come close to filling), depletes local glucose by
up to ~18% before diffusion partially resupplies it (niche construction), and secretes a
diffusing acetate plume — two independently-built simulators talking through one typed port.

investigations.name: cellular-interface
investigations.title: The Cellular Interface
investigations.objective: Can the cellular boundary be specified as nothing but typed, unit-bearing exchange ports (chemical mol·s⁻¹, mechanical N, electrical C·s⁻¹, thermal J·s⁻¹) plus higher-level variables (growth, shape, objective, viability) — with no committed mechanism — and compiled, by installing one conforming handler, into a bounded, goal-directed cell whose interface is exactly the one declared?
investigations.claim: The cell's interface is authored as an inert typed contract and compiled to a running bounded cell; a non-conforming handler that breaks the port contract is rejected at compile time with a CompileError naming the missing ports (Law 1 conformance).

investigations.name: development-and-evolution
investigations.title: Development and Evolution
investigations.objective: Fig 10c–f asks whether two of biology's hardest structural transitions — development (individual cells nesting into a collective composite, a biofilm, with its own shared interface) and evolution (a new interface port switching on, selected by viability) — can be represented as event-driven, compositional rewrites (Law 2′) that preserve the interface underneath them (Law 2). Two composites answer the first half of that (do the drafts compile to executables that run, behind an unchanged interface?) faithfully. This study asks the harder, second half explicitly: how much of what runs is a genuine developmental/evolutionary mechanism, versus a scripted stand-in — and is honest that the paper itself calls this transition "an open and substantial challenge" (line 580).
investigations.claim: Development nests individual cells into a biofilm collective behind a preserved, shared extracellular-matrix interface (Law 2), and evolution switches on a new chemical port under a viability-weighted growth term — both compile and run, and a separate "Live Topology" pair for each even performs genuine runtime place-graph node insertion/removal (in the spirit of Law 2′). But — the defining point of this study — none of this is a validated biological result: selection is a single ODE with fixed viability/fitness constants (not real fitness-based population dynamics), the "new port" is a first-order config-driven ramp (not an emergent evolutionary innovation), the continuous-path biofilm state is a pre-declared, non-inserted scalar store, and even the genuine node-inserting Live-Topology composites run on a fixed wall-clock schedule with a hardcoded mutant fitness advantage rather than an emergent, state-driven trigger. The paper itself calls development and evolution "an open and substantial challenge" (line 580); this study demonstrates the pattern, not the phenomenon.

investigations.name: disintegration
investigations.title: Disintegration
investigations.objective: Fig 6 is disintegration — the change in level of description that fires when a cell crosses its viability bound. Two faces: (a) played through, does the disintegration composite actually show that shift — a thermal shock pushing viability past its bound, viability collapsing, viability-gated metabolism halting, and biomass turning into molecular debris? (b) Is the metabolic-exchange interface at the heart of that same shift realizable at a coarse cell-level grain, an intermediate kinetic grain, and a resolved molecular-network grain (real COBRApy flux-balance optimization) — three grains behind ports that never move?
investigations.claim: Disintegration is a change in level of description made executable and watchable: playing `fig06-disintegration-dynamics`, a thermal shock pushes the cell past its viability bound, viability collapses, viability-gated metabolism halts, and biomass decays into molecular debris (Fig 6a). The same metabolic-exchange interface's cell↔molecular-network equivalence carries three grains behind ports that never move — a coarse lumped yield, a saturating kinetic law, and real COBRApy flux-balance on `e_coli_core` (Fig 6b, Law 4).

investigations.name: disintegration-spatial
investigations.title: Disintegration, Spatial
investigations.objective:
Does Fig 6's level-shift hold spatially -- a coherent CPM cell that loses structural
viability when a diffusing stressor field crosses its bound, its domain resorbing while its
shed material becomes scattering physical particles -- composed from independent frameworks
(viva-cpm + spatio-flux particles) through one coupling process (`CpmDisintegration` +
`BrownianMovement`)?
investigations.claim:
Composing one real CPM cell with a real spatio-flux stressor field and a real spatio-flux
particle-movement process through two coupling processes (`CpmDisintegration` for the
viability-collapse trigger and resorption, stock `BrownianMovement` for the debris scatter)
reproduces Fig 6's level-shift as genuine spatial dissolution, not a scripted or lumped
stand-in for it: over a deterministic 20-tick run, the cell holds coherent (area > 30) through
tick 6, the footprint-local stressor mean crosses viability_threshold at released_tick = 7, the
domain resorbs to area 0 by tick 16, and its 68 shed pixels become a debris cloud whose RMS
spread strictly increases through tick 24 -- hold, cross, resorb, scatter, end to end from one
coupling process plus one stock movement process, mirroring `draft-to-living-cell/disintegration`'s
level-shift pattern (Fig 6) at real spatial, per-pixel resolution.

investigations.name: growth-and-division
investigations.title: Growth and Division
investigations.objective: Does growth — an autocatalytic, energy-coupled DNA-replication process that plays the role of environment-coupled uptake — drive the cell's own dna store across a threshold, and does crossing that threshold fire a genuine structural rewrite of the place graph (one cell node becoming two daughter nodes at runtime, mass conserved) rather than a pre-declared post-structure animated on a wall clock?
investigations.claim: Growth precedes and drives division: an autocatalytic, energy-coupled DNA-replication process grows the cell's own dna store until it crosses a threshold, and crossing that threshold triggers a change to the composition itself — one cell becomes two through a graph rewrite that creates new nodes at runtime and conserves mass (the parent is halved, not doubled), not a pre-drawn pair on a timer (Law 2′, rewrite conformance vs wiring; Law 2, interface preserved across the rewrite).

investigations.name: growth-and-division-spatial
investigations.title: Growth and Division, Spatial
investigations.objective: Does Fig 10a,b's growth-then-divide pattern hold spatially -- a CPM cell whose metabolism (dFBA solved at its own lattice footprint) grows its volume until it crosses a threshold and divides via the native CPM engine operation `divide_cells` (mass-conserved), compounding into a small lineage over the run -- composed from independent frameworks (viva-cpm + spatio-flux + cobra) through one coupling process (`CpmGrowthDivision`)?
investigations.claim: Composing one real CPM cell, growing via real per-footprint dFBA metabolism, with the native CPM engine operation `divide_cells` through a single coupling process (`CpmGrowthDivision`) reproduces Fig 10a,b's growth-then-divide pattern as genuine spatial multicellular compounding, not a scripted lineage or a lumped stand-in for it: over a 36-tick run sampled every 3 ticks, the population steps up in a monotonic non-decreasing staircase (1,2,2,2,4,4,4,8,8,8,13,16), spanning roughly 3-4 generations, while every cell's CPM volume stays bounded in a sawtooth between `reset_target` = 40 and `vol_threshold` = 80 -- growth, crossing, division, and resumed growth in the daughters, all as direct simulation output from three independently-developed frameworks (viva-cpm + spatio-flux + cobra) meeting at one typed interface. This mirrors `draft-to-living-cell/growth-and-division`'s Fig 10a,b claim (growth drives the cell's own state across a threshold; crossing the threshold triggers division) but realizes the division event itself as the native spatial CPM operation `divide_cells` acting directly on lattice pixels, in contrast to that study's place-graph rewrite (one node becoming two structurally-new nodes at a lumped, non-spatial level of composition).

investigations.name: molecular-interfaces
investigations.title: Molecular Interfaces
investigations.objective: At the molecular grain, can a single molecular mechanism (F1Fo ATP synthase) be compiled from its draft and run as a PMF-driven rotary catalyst honoring the four physical interface channels (chemical/electrical/mechanical/thermal) and the specialized substrate/cofactor/catalyst/product ports?
investigations.claim: The molecular interface''s four typed channels compile to a running ATP-synthase mechanism, all four channels driven consistently from one coupled proton flux (chemical_out 0->100; electrical/mechanical/thermal channels move with it) — the molecular level the disintegration study drops into, made concrete. The specialized substrate/cofactor/catalyst/product ports are structurally preserved through compilation but are not driven by this handler (honestly noted, not claimed as dynamic).
